newsitem.title: USA: CME hog and pork belly futures calls mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hog and pork belly futures calls mixed.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from 0.100 cent higher to 0.100 cent lower, with pork bellies called 0.200 cent higher to 0.200 cent lower, analysts said.
Mostly steady cash hog expectations for interior markets and higher pork cutout values should provide some support to nearby hog futures, they said.

But evening up ahead of the Hogs and Pigs report will likely account for the bulk of trade activity. Nearbys should hold near steady while deferred months will likely decline based on the projection for an expanding hog herd, they said.

Analyst estimates on Friday's quarterly report put June 1 all hogs and pigs on U.S. farms at an average 102.9 percent of a year ago and ranged from 101.7 to 105 percent. Estimates on hogs kept for breeding averaged 104.3 percent in a range of 103 to 106 percent and hogs kept for market averaged 102.6 percent of a year ago in a range of 101 to 105 pct.

Nearby pork belly futures were again expected to show strength following the rise in cash belly prices. Cash rose to three week highs Thursday with sales as high as $85 per cwt and expectations are for cash to gain further. Retailer interest is developing as the bacon-lettuce-and-tomato sandwich season approaches, they said.
Next year contracts were again expected to show pressure ahead of the hog report. The report is expected to show increasing hog numbers and larger pork production going into next year, they added.
